metadata.method: Cross-check exact anniversary hooks, preserve superseded IDs and historical source segments, assess institutional dependence and asset rights per story; only core occurrence/date/location marked corroborated.

reviews.title_after: Ireland's Night of the Big Wind begins
reviews.location_after: Ireland, especially the western and northern counties
reviews.evidence_independence: National weather archive versus independent historical editorial; both depend on nineteenth-century eyewitness accounts
reviews.corroborated_core_claim: Met Éireann dates the Night of the Big Wind to January 6–7, 1839, as severe winds spread across Ireland; the overnight peak extends into January 7.
reviews.unverified_cautions: Do not say peak gusts were directly instrument measured, or imply all destruction occurred on January 6; early January 7 was a major period of the storm.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original Irish county impact chronology with a two-date Jan 6–7 band and contemporary document citations

reviews.title_after: The Braer cyclone undergoes extraordinary deepening in the North Atlantic
reviews.location_after: Open North Atlantic between Scotland and Iceland
reviews.evidence_independence: UK Met Office historical index and peer-reviewed storm reanalysis; latter relies on overlapping operational analyses
reviews.corroborated_core_claim: UK Met Office identifies January 10, 1993 as the Braer cyclone date, while published meteorological research documents explosive deepening and an estimated extremely low central pressure near 914 hPa.
reviews.unverified_cautions: 914 hPa is an analyzed cyclone-center pressure, not a UK land-station minimum. Other historic analyses quote different estimates or time references; do not assert an uncontested global all-time ranking.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original pressure-track chart and 24-hour deepening timeline from verified digitized synoptic analysis

reviews.title_after: The great Arctic outbreak of 1899 spreads rare Gulf Coast snow
reviews.location_after: U.S. Southern Plains and northern Gulf Coast
reviews.evidence_independence: Two NOAA/NWS regional climate narratives using overlapping original Weather Bureau observations, not independently measured modern data
reviews.corroborated_core_claim: The Great Arctic Outbreak of February 1899 brought extraordinary cold to the Southern Plains on February 12 and widespread Gulf Coast snow on February 12–13, as documented by regional NWS historical climate analyses.
reviews.unverified_cautions: Do not assign every all-time record low or Gulf Coast snowfall to February 12: some stations recorded minima February 13 and snow continued into February 13. Historical observation sites and time standards require review.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original Feb 12, 1899 surface weather map with explicitly dated temperature/snow observations

reviews.title_after: Halloween 1991 brings a Midwest blizzard as the Perfect Storm churns offshore
reviews.location_after: Upper Midwest, United States; separate northwest Atlantic storm
reviews.evidence_independence: NWS Duluth and NCEI recount the same Midwest episode from NOAA/Weather Bureau observations; the Perfect Storm context is from separate NOAA NESDIS satellite documentation
reviews.corroborated_core_claim: An early-season heavy snowstorm developed across the Upper Midwest on October 31, 1991; NOAA NESDIS separately documents the concurrent northwest Atlantic Perfect Storm and its unusual evolution.
reviews.unverified_cautions: These are two physically distinct storm systems: do not imply the Atlantic nor'easter directly caused the Upper Midwest blizzard. The Perfect Storm peaked in strength October 30, not October 31, and the subsequently unnamed Atlantic hurricane developed later.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original two-panel Oct 31 continental/Atlantic synoptic chart clearly labeling separate lows and snowfall footprint

reviews.title_before: Heavy Snow — CENTRAL ST. LOUIS, Minnesota
reviews.title_after: The Great Blue Norther sends temperatures plunging on 11/11/11
reviews.location_after: Great Plains and Midwestern United States
reviews.evidence_independence: Different NWS climate offices document the same 1911 Weather Bureau station observations; two URLs are not two independent thermometers
reviews.corroborated_core_claim: On November 11, 1911, a powerful cold front swept across the central United States, producing exceptionally rapid temperature falls and some same-day record high and low temperatures.
reviews.unverified_cautions: Record highs/lows use each station's observational day and time basis; Oklahoma City afternoon 83°F and midnight 17°F are historical values needing station-level validation before appearing on a graphic. Do not attribute all regional tornado damage to the front itself.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original plotted Nov 11 hourly or subdaily temperature sequence with historical time/record-source notes

reviews.title_after: Smoke and fog turn Interstate 75 into a zero-visibility danger near Gainesville
reviews.location_after: Paynes Prairie and Interstate 75 near Gainesville, Florida
reviews.second_source_publisher: CBS/AP based on Florida highway investigation
reviews.evidence_independence: Independent news coverage of state highway investigation corroborates crash/date; NCEI wildfire narrative and news sources share police accounts
reviews.corroborated_core_claim: On January 29, 2012, wildfire smoke mixed with fog near Paynes Prairie, causing extremely poor visibility during deadly multiple-vehicle crashes on Interstate 75.
reviews.unverified_cautions: NCEI classifies original event as WILDFIRE, though this editorial story focuses on smoke-fog visibility; collision liability, precise crash counts and final death totals need separate original Florida investigation checks. Do not infer arson or make unsupported cause-of-fire claims.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original Paynes Prairie terrain/smoke-source and highway fog-timing diagram using verified observation time bases

reviews.title_after: An EF4 tornado tears through Lone Grove during the 2009 Oklahoma outbreak
reviews.evidence_independence: NWS Norman storm survey is original source behind NCEI Wilson segment; same survey, not independent wind evidence
reviews.corroborated_core_claim: NWS Norman confirms the February 10, 2009 Lone Grove EF4 tornado, with the original Wilson NCEI location representing one segment of the multijurisdictional tornado.
reviews.unverified_cautions: The Wilson county/area segment is not a second EF4 tornado. NWS GIS track centerline and EF-rated survey points are approximate; wind speeds are damage-survey estimates. Do not sum regional casualties across county segments.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original tornado-track map with mapped EF-damage points and warning products labeled separately

reviews.title_after: Freezing rain creates dangerous elevated-roadway ice before Fort Worth's I-35W pileup
reviews.evidence_independence: Independent federal highway investigation reviews roadway monitoring and conditions, distinct from NCEI meteorological storm record; shared weather station inputs possible
reviews.corroborated_core_claim: The NTSB dates the Fort Worth I-35W multi-vehicle crash to the morning of February 11, 2021 and documents icy elevated lanes during freezing rain and mist.
reviews.unverified_cautions: The NTSB found deficiencies in roadway monitoring and management as contributing factors, not icy weather acting alone. The later February 14–17 Texas winter storm is a distinct phase, and neither event should inherit the other's weather observations.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original bridge-surface-temperature/precipitation timeline juxtaposed with NTSB chronology, separating observations from investigative inferences

reviews.title_after: A late-night EF3 tornado strikes Brunswick County's Ocean Ridge community
reviews.location_after: Ocean Ridge Plantation and southwestern Brunswick County, North Carolina
reviews.evidence_independence: NCEI Grissettown segment and NWS Wilmington detailed page stem from the same NWS damage survey
reviews.corroborated_core_claim: NWS Wilmington confirms a long-track EF3 tornado on February 15, 2021 through Brunswick County, including the Ocean Ridge Plantation area; Grissettown is a storm-report location within the broader event.
reviews.unverified_cautions: 160-mph peak wind is damage-derived, not an anemometer gust. Distinguish the tornado itself from separate straight-line/microburst damage documented to its north; path-width and fatalities belong to exact surveyed storm.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original Brunswick County track-and-radar timeline, isolating Ocean Ridge and separate microburst reports

reviews.title_after: The Kissimmee F3 tornado strikes during Florida's deadly overnight outbreak
reviews.evidence_independence: NWS Melbourne tornado assessment is the original survey that informs the NCEI Intercession City report
reviews.corroborated_core_claim: NWS Melbourne documents a major Central Florida tornado outbreak late February 22 into early February 23, 1998; NCEI's Intercession City F3 belongs to the Kissimmee-track tornado on February 23.
reviews.unverified_cautions: Use the pre-2007 F3 rating rather than EF3. Survey fatalities in Kissimmee (individual tornado) must not be conflated with all outbreak fatalities. Exact local midnight timing varies by storm.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original 22–23 February Florida surveyed-track overlay with Kissimmee tornado highlighted and time zone noted

reviews.title_after: A violent F4 tornado crosses Benton and the southern Little Rock area
reviews.evidence_independence: Same historical NWS damage survey and NCEI record, source count does not equal independent tornado observations
reviews.corroborated_core_claim: NWS Little Rock documents a March 1, 1997 F4 tornado crossing from southeast of Benton through Shannon Hills and southern Little Rock, one of two major F4 tornadoes from the Interstate 30 supercell.
reviews.unverified_cautions: Two major F4 paths from one supercell are separate tornadoes. Do not attribute entire 17-tornado statewide outbreak casualties to the Benton–Little Rock F4. Original F rating, not EF.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original Interstate 30 supercell's two F4 path map plus local radar rotation timeline

reviews.title_after: Dense fog contributes to a multi-vehicle Interstate 57 pileup near Charleston
reviews.location_after: Interstate 57 near Charleston, Mississippi County, Missouri
reviews.second_source_publisher: KFVS reporting Missouri State Highway Patrol records
reviews.evidence_independence: Regional contemporaneous reporting quotes state patrol crash reports and emergency responders; not an independent instrument visibility measurement
reviews.corroborated_core_claim: Police and emergency response reporting dates multiple large Interstate 57 crashes near Charleston, Missouri to March 17, 2022 in dense fog, consistent with NCEI's Mississippi County zone entry.
reviews.unverified_cautions: Preliminary vehicle counts differed (33, 50 or more), and final fatalities/injuries must be reconciled to case-level police reports. Some smoke observed was from post-crash vehicle fires; do NOT label this a wildfire smoke-fog event.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original route/weather visibility timeline with all crash counts flagged pending official final reconciliations

reviews.title_after: An F3 tornado strikes Newbern during the 2006 Mid-South outbreak
reviews.location_after: Newbern and Dyer County, northwestern Tennessee
reviews.evidence_independence: NWS Memphis storm-survey documentation and NCEI Newbern entry are the same underlying survey, not independent casualty evidence
reviews.corroborated_core_claim: NWS Memphis documents an F3 tornado impacting Dyer County and Newbern on April 2, 2006 during a larger multi-state tornado outbreak.
reviews.unverified_cautions: Use historical F3, not EF3; individual Dyer County fatalities and injuries are not necessarily the multistate outbreak total. Check daylight-saving/CST product times before any timeline visualization.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original Newbern Dyer County surveyed path, severe-weather products, and multiple local time conventions annotated

reviews.title_after: Lightning ignites the Yarnell Hill wildfire in Arizona
reviews.evidence_independence: NWS Flagstaff independent retrospective fire-weather reconstruction includes original lightning data; NCEI event description likely shares incident reports
reviews.corroborated_core_claim: NWS Flagstaff documents lightning in the Yarnell vicinity on June 28, 2013, when the Yarnell Hill Fire ignited; its catastrophic run during a thunderstorm-outflow wind shift occurred two days later on June 30.
reviews.unverified_cautions: Do not assign the loss of 19 Granite Mountain Hotshots to June 28; deaths occurred June 30. NWS nearby lightning detection is not a geolocated observation of the exact ignition channel. Fire spread and timing on June 30 require the investigation's separate record.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original three-day lightning/heat and June30 outflow timing diagram with distinct dates

reviews.title_after: An unusual F2 tornado tears through downtown Salt Lake City
reviews.evidence_independence: NCEI Salt Lake City reporting and NWS city tornado history trace to the same 1999 tornado damage survey
reviews.corroborated_core_claim: NWS Salt Lake City documents an F2 tornado crossing downtown Salt Lake City on August 11, 1999, causing substantial downtown damage.
reviews.unverified_cautions: Use historic F2 Fujita rather than EF2. The NWS mapped damage-intensity gradient and track centerline must not be presented as modern high-resolution radar measurements; archival third-party building photographs are not automatically cleared for reuse.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original F2 track through downtown city blocks and damage clusters, using NWS surveyed coordinates with original redraw

reviews.title_after: Intense snow bands bury New York City during the February 2006 blizzard
reviews.location_after: New York City and lower Hudson Valley, New York
reviews.second_source_publisher: New York City Mayor's Office (contemporaneous release)
reviews.evidence_independence: NWS regional mesoscale snow analysis and contemporary municipal emergency announcement are distinct institutions but rely on some common snowfall observations
reviews.corroborated_core_claim: An intense Northeast winter storm culminated on February 12, 2006, with exceptional snowfall in New York City and record-status reporting at the time.
reviews.unverified_cautions: The 26.9-inch 2006 Central Park tally was called a record then; later storms may surpass it (a February 2026 NYC event is reported at 27.5 inches). Do not describe 2006 as the unqualified current all-time record. Snowband rates require exact source-time verification.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original NYC snowfall transect and hourly mesoscale frontogenesis radar depiction

reviews.title_after: Oroville Dam's emergency spillway crisis prompts evacuations
reviews.location_after: Oroville and downstream Feather River communities, California
reviews.second_source_publisher: U.S. Geological Survey / AGU hydrologic article
reviews.evidence_independence: California DWR engineering/emergency chronology plus USGS hydrologic context written after the incident; USGS largely repeats reported evacuation timing
reviews.corroborated_core_claim: On February 12, 2017, erosion threatening the Oroville Dam emergency spillway led to mandatory evacuation warnings/orders downstream, after weeks of runoff and elevated reservoir inflow.
reviews.unverified_cautions: Dam-breach catastrophe was feared but DID NOT OCCUR. Do not label February 12 as a measured natural downstream flood disaster, or claim the rainfall on February 12 itself caused all erosion; major storms occurred earlier. Engineering mechanisms are separate from meteorological forcing.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original reservoir elevation/emergency spillway timeline with dates of preceding storms and February 12 evacuation action
